claim.claim-text: 1. A mechanism to controllably move a wire within a flexible tubular member, the wire including opposed wire ends extending outwardly of a proximal end of the flexible tubular member, comprising:
a drive mechanism; a coupling located between the drive mechanism and the wire end, wherein movement of the coupling in the direction of the wire end results in opposed motion of the wire end.

2. The mechanism of claim 1, wherein the coupling further comprises a fulcrum having a fixed location with respect to the proximal end of the flexible tubular member, and a lever having a first end, a second end, and a pivoting connection with the fulcrum therebetween.
3. The mechanism of claim 2, wherein the coupling further comprises a plunger extending from the first end of the lever, preferably wherein a wire end is connected to the second end of the lever..

4. The mechanism of claim 3, further comprising an adaptor housing positioned between the drive mechanism and the proximal end of the flexible tubular member, the adaptor including at least one bore extending therethrough; and a bushing reciprocally moveable within the at least one bore, wherein an end of the bushing is connected to the plunger.

5. The mechanism of claim 1, wherein the coupling further comprises a fulcrum having a fixed location with respect to the proximal end of the flexible tubular member, and a lever having a first side, a second side, and a pivoting connection with the fulcrum located between the first side of the lever and the second side of the lever.
6. The mechanism of claim 5, wherein the coupling further comprises a plunger extending from the first side of the lever,

preferably further comprising an adaptor housing positioned between the drive mechanism and the proximal end of the flexible tubular member, the adaptor including at least one bore extending therethrough; and a bushing reciprocally moveable within the at least one bore, wherein an end of the bushing is connected to the plunger.
7. The mechanism of claim 6, wherein a wire end is connected to the second side of the lever.

8. The mechanism of claim 1, further comprising an adaptor housing positioned between the drive mechanism and the proximal end of the flexible tubular member; and a fulcrum extending from the adaptor, and a lever having a first side, a second side, and a pivoting connection with the fulcrum between the first side of the lever and the second side of the lever, preferably wherein the adaptor including a plunger extending from the first side of the lever and a wire end connected to the second side thereof.
9. A mechanism to controllably move a wire within a flexible tubular member, the wire including opposed wire ends extending outwardly of a proximal end of the flexible tubular member, comprising:

a housing; a fulcrum extending from the housing, and a lever having a first side and an opposed second side, rotatably connected to the fulcrum at a location between the first side of the lever and the opposed second side of the lever.
10. The mechanism of claim 9, further comprising a plunger connected to the first side of the lever and a wire end connected to the second side of the lever.
11. The mechanism of claim 10, further comprising:
a bore extending inwardly of the housing; a bushing disposed in the bore, the bushing sized to be capable of reciprocating motion within the bore, wherein the bushing is connected to the plunger.
12. The mechanism of claim 11, further comprising:
13. The mechanism of claim 12, wherein the bushing comprises opposed ends, and a recess extending inwardly of one of the opposed ends.
14. The mechanism of claim 13, further comprising a magnetic material disposed inwardly of the recess.
15. The mechanism of claim 14, wherein the wire actuation member further comprises a magnetic material, preferably wherein the magnetic material comprises one of a magnet or a ferromagnetic material.
